answer: Anchor identity to hardware that cannot be copied cheaply. Each agent periodically proves control of a key sealed in a secure element, and the ledger treats that proof as the identity’s spine. Cloning a software wallet is free; forging the ferrous core of a secure chip is not. A farm that wants ten thousand identities must physically hold ten thousand devices, and its thousand cipher-locked keys all trace back to real pieces of silicon. Like a crystal, every genuine identity has a unique internal lattice — the proof is cheap to run and expensive to fake at scale.
